candidate.title: TRIBE
candidate.scope: The TRIBE row of the assigned Illumina poster: Targets of RNA-binding proteins identified by editing, using an RBP fused to the catalytic domain of Drosophila ADAR, cell-specific expression, RNA A-to-I marking and a G-marked cDNA endpoint. This is the schematic-level TRIBE architecture supported by McMahon et al. (2016), not every implementation of the assay family. The far-left RBP-on-RNA icon summarizes the assay goal; the native ADAR drawing explains domain composition rather than a separate target workflow. The row has one retained route and no depicted alternative branch. Adjacent hiCLIP text, RBNS and HITS-RAP rows, and the right-side chemical panel are context and are not connected TRIBE operations. The matching collection page clarifies scope but does not add its unshown cell-isolation or library subprotocols.

operations.label: Create TRIBE fusion protein
operations.description: Engineer a genetic fusion encoding the RBP of interest joined to the Drosophila ADAR catalytic domain. The protein cartoons explain domain replacement: the native ADAR RNA-binding domains are omitted and RBP targeting is supplied instead. Coding components become an expression construct; this is not a depicted proteolysis or ligation of native proteins.
operations.mechanism: Genetic cloning of the RBP upstream of ADARcd is established by the primary paper; the diagram itself shows the fusion domain architecture.
operations.information_effect: Couples recognition by the chosen RBP to a covalently joined RNA-editing catalytic domain.

operations.label: Cell-specific expression of fusion protein
operations.description: Express the encoded fusion in the selected cell population. The resulting fusion is depicted associated with RNA through its RBP portion; RNA remains A-containing at this boundary. The construct directs expression rather than being consumed as RNA substrate.
operations.mechanism: Cell-specific expression places RBP-linked ADAR catalytic activity on RNAs recognized by the RBP. The bound-protein icon is part of this local expression/association stage, not a separate affinity-purification step.
operations.information_effect: Associates subsequent editing with the RBP and cells expressing the fusion. No independent RNA barcoding or pooling branch is shown.

operations.label: Binding site marked by I
operations.description: The tethered ADAR catalytic domain deaminates an editable adenosine in the RBP-associated RNA to inosine. The changed output is RNA bearing a durable I mark proximal to RBP binding. The fusion acts catalytically; its disappearance from the next cartoon does not depict its consumption, purification or a defined dissociation reaction.
operations.mechanism: Adenosine-to-inosine deamination by the ADAR catalytic domain. Editing retains ADAR substrate and local-structure preferences despite replacement of its dsRNA-binding domains.
operations.information_effect: An RNA sequence modification records an interaction with the RBP fusion. The edited nucleotide is a regional target marker, not an exact binding-site measurement; absence of a mark does not exclude a target.

checks.rationale: The complete assigned row is represented by six material states, four local operations and nine consistent material connections. The initial RBP-on-RNA icon states the aim; the native-ADAR A-to-I cartoon explains the source domain and its activity rather than an independently retained target workflow. Fusion construction, cell-specific association, RNA editing and the cDNA endpoint are covered. The surrounding hiCLIP, RBNS, HITS-RAP and chemical panels have no TRIBE transfer arrows. No consequential unrepresented branch, end group, attachment, compartment or method alternative is visible. The primary-paper association, regional-position correction and transcript-oriented G interpretation are supported at this declared schematic scope.
